opening: Buck did not read the newspapers, or he would have known that trouble was brewing, not alone for himself, but for every tide-water dog, strong of muscle and with warm, long hair, from Puget Sound to San Diego.
about: 캘리포니아의 판사 집에서 편하게 살던 개 벅이 금광 열풍 속에서 북쪽 땅의 썰매개로 끌려가는 이야기다. 문명의 울타리를 벗어난 개의 눈으로 본능과 생존을 따라가 볼 수 있다.
aboutEn: Buck, a dog living comfortably on a California judge's estate, is swept up in the Klondike gold rush and drawn north as a sled dog. Seen through a dog's eyes, the story invites you to think about instinct and survival once the comforts of civilization are gone.

title: 데미안
author: 헤르만 헤세
opening: In order to tell my story, I must begin far back. If it were possible, I should have to go back much further still, to the earliest years of my childhood, and even beyond, to my distant ancestry.
about: 에밀 싱클레어라는 인물이 자신의 어린 시절부터 스스로 되돌아보며 들려주는 성장 이야기다. 남들이 정해 준 길 대신 자기 안의 목소리를 따라 사는 일이 왜 그토록 어려운지 생각하게 한다.
aboutEn: Emil Sinclair looks back on his youth, beginning far back in his childhood, to tell the story of his own growth. It makes you ask why living by the promptings of one's true self is so difficult.

title: 댈러웨이 부인
author: 버지니아 울프
opening: For Lucy had her work cut out for her. The doors would be taken off their hinges; Rumpelmayer's men were coming. And then, thought Clarissa Dalloway, what a morning—fresh as if issued to children on a beach. What a lark! What a plunge!
about: 클라리사 댈러웨이가 직접 꽃을 사러 나서는 6월 어느 아침에서 시작하는 소설이다. 거리의 풍경과 과거의 기억이 한 인물의 의식 속에서 자연스럽게 이어지는 문장을 따라가는 즐거움이 있다.
aboutEn: The novel opens on a June morning as Clarissa Dalloway sets out to buy the flowers herself. Its pleasure lies in sentences that move easily between the street around her and her memories, all within one mind.

title: 해는 또다시 떠오른다
author: 어니스트 헤밍웨이
opening: Robert Cohn was once middleweight boxing champion of Princeton. Do not think that I am very much impressed by that as a boxing title, but it meant a lot to Cohn.
about: 프린스턴 출신 복서 로버트 콘을 소개하는 화자의 목소리로 시작해 전쟁 뒤 유럽에서 지내는 사람들을 그린 소설이다. 짧고 절제된 문장 속에서 '잃어버린 세대'라는 말이 무엇을 가리키는지 헤아려 볼 수 있다.
aboutEn: Narrated by a voice that begins by introducing Robert Cohn, a former Princeton boxing champion, this novel follows a circle of people living in Europe after the war. Its spare, restrained prose lets you consider what the phrase "a lost generation" means.

title: 무기여 잘 있거라
author: 어니스트 헤밍웨이
opening: In the late summer of that year we lived in a house in a village that looked across the river and the plain to the mountains. In the bed of the river there were pebbles and boulders, dry and white in the sun, and the water was clear and swiftly moving and blue in the channels.
about: 전쟁 중 강과 들판 너머로 산이 보이는 마을에 머물던 한 병사가 그해 늦여름을 회상하며 시작하는 소설이다. 행군하는 군대와 먼지 쌓인 길을 담담하게 그려 낸 문장이 전쟁의 분위기를 전한다.
aboutEn: A soldier recalls the late summer he spent in a village looking across a river and plain to the mountains, with troops marching by during the war. The plain, matter-of-fact description of dust, roads and marching men conveys the atmosphere of war.

title: 젊은 예술가의 초상
author: 제임스 조이스
match: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man
original: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man
opening: Once upon a time and a very good time it was there was a moocow coming down along the road and this moocow that was coming down along the road met a nicens little boy named baby tuckoo.... His father told him that story: his father looked at him through a glass: he had a hairy face.
about: 아기 스티븐 디덜러스가 아버지가 들려주는 이야기를 듣는 가장 어린 기억에서 출발해 학교생활로 이어지는 성장 소설이다. 어린아이의 감각으로 쓴 문장이 점점 달라지는 과정을 따라가는 재미가 있다.
aboutEn: This coming-of-age novel begins with the infant Stephen Dedalus hearing a story from his father, then moves on to his school days. You can enjoy watching the child's sensory, simple language gradually change as he grows.

title: 스완네 집 쪽으로
author: 마르셀 프루스트
opening: I would ask myself what o'clock it could be; I could hear the whistling of trains, which, now nearer and now farther off, punctuating the distance like the note of a bird in a forest, shewed me in perspective the deserted countryside through which a traveller would be hurrying towards the nearest st
about: 「잃어버린 시간을 찾아서」의 첫 권으로, 오랫동안 일찍 잠자리에 들곤 했다는 화자의 회상으로 시작한다. 잠들기 전후의 의식과 기억이 길게 이어지는 문장을 읽으며 시간과 기억을 생각하게 된다.
aboutEn: The first volume of Remembrance of Things Past opens with a narrator recalling how he used to go to bed early. Its long, flowing sentences about the mind between waking and sleep invite reflection on time and memory.

title: 젊은 베르테르의 슬픔
author: 요한 볼프강 폰 괴테
opening: I have carefully collected whatever I have been able to learn of the story of poor Werther, and here present it to you, knowing that you will thank me for it. To his spirit and character you cannot refuse your admiration and love: to his fate you will not deny your tears.
about: 베르테르라는 젊은이가 친구에게 보내는 편지로 이어지는 소설로, 편집자가 모은 기록이라는 틀을 갖고 있다. 한 사람의 마음이 편지 속에서 어떻게 드러나는지를 가까이에서 지켜볼 수 있다.
aboutEn: This novel unfolds through letters a young man named Werther writes to a friend, framed as a record gathered by an editor. It lets you watch closely as one person's inner feelings come through in his own words.

title: 베니스에서의 죽음
author: 토마스 만
opening: On a spring afternoon of the year 19—, when our continent lay under such threatening weather for whole months, Gustav Aschenbach, or von Aschenbach as his name read officially after his fiftieth birthday, had left his apartment on the Prinzregentenstrasse in Munich and had gone for a long walk.
about: 뮌헨에 사는 오십 대 작가 아센바흐가 어느 봄날 오후 산책에 나서면서 시작되는 토마스 만의 중편이다.
aboutEn:
Thomas Mann's novella opens as Gustav Aschenbach, an author in his fifties, sets out on a spring afternoon walk in Munich.
It invites you to watch how a disciplined writer's life of the will begins to shift.

title: 개를 데리고 다니는 부인 외
author: 안톤 체호프
match: The Lady with the Dog and Other Stories
original: The Lady with the Dog and Other Stories
opening: IT was said that a new person had appeared on the sea-front: a lady with a little dog. Dmitri Dmitritch Gurov, who had by then been a fortnight at Yalta, and so was fairly at home there, had begun to take an interest in new arrivals.
about: 얄타 해변에서 흰 스피츠를 데리고 다니는 젊은 부인을 눈여겨보는 유부남 구로프를 그린 체호프의 단편집이다.
aboutEn:
This Chekhov collection begins at Yalta, where the married Gurov notices a young woman walking a small white dog.
Its plain, quiet telling shows how much a few ordinary details can say about a person.

title: 아버지와 아들
author: 이반 투르게네프
opening: In this masterly unromantic novel, Turgenev drew a character, Bazarov, who served to express what he taught us to call Nihilism, and made a movement into a man. In Russia itself the effect of the story was astonishing. The portrait of Bazarov was immediately and angrily resented as a cold travesty.
about: 허무주의자 청년 바자로프와 구세대 귀족 페트로비치 가문을 다룬 투르게네프의 장편소설이다.
aboutEn:
Turgenev's novel centers on the young nihilist Bazarov and the older generation of the Petrovitch family.
It shows a clash between generations that angered both the radicals and the old aristocrats of its day.

title: 필경사 바틀비
author: 허먼 멜빌
match: Bartleby, the Scrivener: A Story of Wall-Street
opening: I am a rather elderly man. The nature of my avocations for the last thirty years has brought me into more than ordinary contact with what would seem an interesting and somewhat singular set of men, of whom as yet nothing that I know of has ever been written:—I mean the law-copyists or scriveners.
about: 월스트리트 법률 사무소를 운영하는 나이 지긋한 화자가 가장 기이한 필경사 바틀비를 회고하는 멜빌의 단편이다.
aboutEn:
An elderly Wall Street lawyer narrates his memory of Bartleby, the strangest law-copyist he ever knew, in this Melville tale.
The narrator admits how little can be known of the man, which leaves you wondering what a person owes to another.

title: 이선 프롬
author: 이디스 워튼
opening: If you know Starkfield, Massachusetts, you know the post-office. If you know the post-office you must have seen Ethan Frome drive up to it, drop the reins on his hollow-backed bay and drag himself across the brick pavement to the white colonnade; and you must have asked who he was.
about: 매사추세츠 스타크필드에서 절름발이로 지내는 이선 프롬의 사연을 한 외부인이 조각조각 모아 전하는 소설이다.
aboutEn:
A visitor to Starkfield, Massachusetts, pieces together the story of Ethan Frome, a lame and weathered man, from what various townspeople tell him.
The narrator admits each telling differed, so you may ask whose version of a life to trust.

title: 순수의 시대
author: 이디스 워튼
opening: Though there was already talk of the erection, in remote metropolitan distances "above the Forties," of a new Opera House which should compete in costliness and splendour with those of the great European capitals, the world of fashion was still content to reassemble every winter in the shabby red an
about: 1870년대 초 뉴욕, 아카데미 오브 뮤직의 오페라 공연 밤으로 시작하는 이디스 워튼의 장편소설이다.
aboutEn:
Edith Wharton's novel opens at an opera night at New York's Academy of Music in the early 1870s.
Its opening pages describe the manners of old fashionable society with dry wit, setting the rules its characters live by.

title: 나사의 회전
author: 헨리 제임스
opening: The story had held us, round the fire, sufficiently breathless, but except the obvious remark that it was gruesome, as, on Christmas Eve in an old house, a strange tale should essentially be, I remember no comment uttered till somebody happened to say that it was the only case he had met in which su
about: 크리스마스 이브에 난롯가에 모인 사람들이 아이들에게 나타난 유령 이야기를 듣는 데서 시작하는 헨리 제임스의 중편이다.
aboutEn:
Henry James's novella begins on Christmas Eve, as guests around a fire hear a ghost story involving children.
The framing of a story told within a story makes you attend closely to who is speaking and how far to trust them.

title: 설득
author: 제인 오스틴
opening: Sir Walter Elliot, of Kellynch Hall, in Somersetshire, was a man who, for his own amusement, never took up any book but the Baronetage; there he found occupation for an idle hour, and consolation in a distressed one; there his faculties were roused into admiration and respect, by contemplating the l
about: 준남작 월터 엘리엇 경과 그의 딸들을 소개하며 시작하는 제인 오스틴의 소설이다.
aboutEn:
Jane Austen's novel begins by introducing Sir Walter Elliot of Kellynch Hall and his daughters.
The opening shows his vanity through his fondness for the Baronetage, and Austen's gently ironic eye is on display from the first page.

title: 테스
author: 토머스 하디
match: Tess of the d'Urbervilles: A Pure Woman
opening: The main portion of the following story appeared—with slight modifications—in the Graphic newspaper; other chapters, more especially addressed to adult readers, in the Fortnightly Review and the National Observer, as episodic sketches.
about: 가난한 시골 처녀 테스가 자신이 오랜 귀족 가문의 후손이라는 사실을 알게 된 뒤 겪는 삶을 그린 하디의 소설이다.
aboutEn: Hardy's novel follows Tess, a poor country girl who learns she descends from an old noble family, and the life that follows.

title: 바스커빌가의 개
author: 아서 코난 도일
opening: Mr. Sherlock Holmes, who was usually very late in the mornings, save upon those not infrequent occasions when he was up all night, was seated at the breakfast table. I stood upon the hearth-rug and picked up the stick which our visitor had left behind him the night before.
about: 의사 모티머가 두고 간 지팡이를 단서로 홈스가 방문객을 추리하며 바스커빌 가문의 저주 사건이 시작된다.
aboutEn: Holmes deduces the visitor from a stick Dr. Mortimer left behind, opening the case of the Baskerville family curse.

title: 주홍색 연구
author: 아서 코난 도일
opening: In the year 1878 I took my degree of Doctor of Medicine of the University of London, and proceeded to Netley to go through the course prescribed for surgeons in the army. Having completed my studies there, I was duly attached to the Fifth Northumberland Fusiliers as Assistant Surgeon.
about: 아프간 전쟁에서 부상당한 군의관 왓슨이 셜록 홈스를 만나 함께 사건을 맡게 되는, 홈스 시리즈의 첫 작품이다.
aboutEn: The first Holmes tale, in which Watson, a surgeon wounded in the Afghan war, meets Sherlock Holmes and joins his investigation.

title: 오페라의 유령
author: 가스통 르루
opening: The Opera ghost really existed. He was not, as was long believed, a creature of the imagination of the artists, the superstition of the managers, or a product of the absurd and impressionable brains of the young ladies of the ballet, their mothers, the box-keepers, the cloak-room attendants or the c
about: 파리 오페라 극장에 나타난다는 유령이 실존했다는 화자의 주장으로 시작해 극장을 둘러싼 괴이한 사건을 따라간다.
aboutEn: The narrator claims the Paris Opera ghost really existed, and the book traces the strange events surrounding the opera house.

title: 아르센 뤼팽
author: 모리스 르블랑
opening: The rays of the September sun flooded the great halls of the old château of the Dukes of Charmerace, lighting up with their mellow glow the spoils of so many ages and many lands, jumbled together with the execrable taste which so often afflicts those whose only standard of value is money.
about: 공작 가문의 오래된 성을 배경으로, 백만장자의 딸과 도난 사건, 괴도 뤼팽을 둘러싼 이야기가 펼쳐지는 소설이다.
aboutEn: Set in a Duke's old château, this novel weaves together a millionaire's daughter, a series of thefts, and the gentleman thief Lupin.

title: 노트르담 드 파리
author: 빅토르 위고
opening: These Greek capitals, black with age, and quite deeply graven in the stone, with I know not what signs peculiar to Gothic caligraphy imprinted upon their forms and upon their attitudes, as though with the purpose of revealing that it had been a hand of the Middle Ages which had inscribed them there,
about: 작가가 노트르담 탑에서 발견한 벽의 낙서에서 출발해, 중세 파리와 대성당에 얽힌 운명의 이야기를 풀어내는 소설이다.
aboutEn: Starting from a word the author found carved in a Notre-Dame tower, this novel tells of fate in medieval Paris and its cathedral.

title: 삼총사
author: 알렉상드르 뒤마
opening: In which it is proved that, notwithstanding their names' ending in os and is, the heroes of the story which we are about to have the honor to relate to our readers have nothing mythological about them.
about: 시골 청년 다르타냥이 파리로 올라와 국왕의 총사들과 얽히며 모험을 시작하는 뒤마의 역사 활극이다.
aboutEn: Dumas's historical adventure follows the young D'Artagnan, who comes to Paris and becomes entangled with the King's musketeers.

title: 고리오 영감
author: 오노레 드 발자크
opening: Mme. Vauquer (nee de Conflans) is an elderly person, who for the past forty years has kept a lodging-house in the Rue Nueve-Sainte-Genevieve, in the district that lies between the Latin Quarter and the Faubourg Saint-Marcel.
about: 1819년 파리의 하숙집 보케르관에 모인 사람들을 통해 당시 파리의 삶을 세밀하게 그린 발자크의 소설이다.
aboutEn: Balzac's novel portrays Paris life in 1819 through the residents of Mme. Vauquer's boarding house.

title: 제르미날
author: 에밀 졸라
opening: To-day, when critics view Zola In the main with indifference rather than with horror, although he still retains his popular favour, the distinction of Germinal is yet more clearly recognized.
about: 프랑스 북부 탄광촌을 무대로 광부들의 가혹한 노동과 파업을 그린 에밀 졸라의 소설이다.
aboutEn: Émile Zola's novel portrays the harsh labor and the strike of miners in a coal-mining district of northern France.','

title: 적과 흑
author: 스탕달
match: The Red and the Black: A Chronicle of 1830
opening: Henri Beyle was born in 1783 in Grenoble in Dauphiny, the son of a royalist lawyer, situated on the borderland between the gentry and that bourgeoisie which our author was subsequently to chastise with that malice peculiar to those who spring themselves from the class which they despise.
about: 야심 찬 청년 쥘리앵 소렐이 출세를 노리며 사회를 헤쳐 가는 스탕달의 소설이다.
aboutEn: Stendhal's novel follows Julien Sorel, an ambitious young man who tries to make his way up in society.

title: 올리버 트위스트
author: 찰스 디킨스
opening: Among other public buildings in a certain town, which for many reasons it will be prudent to refrain from mentioning, and to which I will assign no fictitious name, there is one anciently common to most towns, great or small: to wit, a workhouse; and in this workhouse was born; on a day and date whi
about: 구빈원에서 태어난 고아 소년 올리버 트위스트가 런던에서 겪는 일을 그린 디킨스의 소설이다.
aboutEn: Dickens's novel follows Oliver Twist, an orphan born in a workhouse, through his troubles in London.

title: 데이비드 코퍼필드
author: 찰스 디킨스
opening: I do not find it easy to get sufficiently far away from this Book, in the first sensations of having finished it, to refer to it with the composure which this formal heading would seem to require.
about: 주인공 데이비드가 태어나 자라며 겪은 일을 직접 들려주는 디킨스의 성장 소설이다.
aboutEn: Dickens's novel of growing up, in which David Copperfield tells the story of his own birth and early life.

title: 허영의 시장
author: 윌리엄 메이크피스 새커리
opening: As the manager of the Performance sits before the curtain on the boards and looks into the Fair, a feeling of profound melancholy comes over him in his survey of the bustling place.
about: 인형극 무대를 연 극단 주인의 서문으로 시작해, 허영으로 들끓는 세상을 그린 새커리의 소설이다.
aboutEn: Thackeray's novel opens with a showman's preface and depicts a world bustling with vanity, likened to a fair.

title: 남과 북
author: 엘리자베스 개스켈
opening: But as Margaret half suspected, Edith had fallen asleep. She lay curled up on the sofa in the back drawing-room in Harley Street looking very lovely in her white muslin and blue ribbons.
about: 마거릿이라는 젊은 여성이 사촌 이디스의 결혼을 앞두고 있는 런던 장면에서 시작하는 개스켈의 소설이다.
aboutEn: Gaskell's novel opens in London, where a young woman named Margaret watches her cousin Edith prepare for marriage.

title: 로드 짐
author: 조지프 콘래드
opening: When this novel first appeared in book form a notion got about that I had been bolted away with. Some reviewers maintained that the work starting as a short story had got beyond the writer's control. One or two discovered internal evidence of the fact, which seemed to amuse them.
about: 순례선 사건에서 비롯된 한 선원의 이야기를 말로가 들려주는 방식으로 풀어 가는 콘래드의 소설이다.
aboutEn: Conrad's novel tells of a seaman through Marlow's narration, starting from an incident aboard a pilgrim ship.

title: 아들과 연인
author: D. H. 로런스
opening: "The Bottoms" succeeded to "Hell Row". Hell Row was a block of thatched, bulging cottages that stood by the brookside on Greenhill Lane. There lived the colliers who worked in the little gin-pits two fields away.
about: 노팅엄셔 탄광촌 베스트우드에서 광부 모렐 가족이 꾸려 가는 결혼 생활과 아이들의 성장을 그린 소설이다.
aboutEn: This novel follows the Morel family, a miner's household in the Nottinghamshire colliery village of Bestwood, through marriage and childhood.  ———

title: 나의 안토니아
author: 윌라 캐더
opening: Last summer I happened to be crossing the plains of Iowa in a season of intense heat, and it was my good fortune to have for a traveling companion James Quayle Burden—Jim Burden, as we still call him in the West.
about: 네브래스카 대평원에서 자란 짐 버든이 어린 시절 만난 이민 소녀 안토니아를 회고하는 소설이다.
aboutEn: Jim Burden looks back on his Nebraska prairie childhood and Ántonia, the immigrant girl he met there. Readers can see how the plains and the people who settled them shape one man's memory.

title: 메인 스트리트
author: 싱클레어 루이스
opening: The town is, in our tale, called "Gopher Prairie, Minnesota." But its Main Street is the continuation of Main Streets everywhere. The story would be the same in Ohio or Montana, in Kansas or Kentucky or Illinois, and not very differently would it be told Up York State or in the Carolina hills.
about: 미네소타의 작은 마을 고퍼 프레이리를 무대로 한 미국 소도시 풍속 소설이다.
aboutEn: This novel is set in Gopher Prairie, Minnesota, a small Midwestern town that stands for Main Streets everywhere. It invites you to ask how much a town's comfortable habits and shared faith shut out other ways of living.

title: 마틴 에덴
author: 잭 런던
opening: The one opened the door with a latch-key and went in, followed by a young fellow who awkwardly removed his cap. He wore rough clothes that smacked of the sea, and he was manifestly out of place in the spacious hall in which he found himself.
about: 바다 냄새 나는 거친 젊은이 마틴 에덴이 처음 상류층 저택에 발을 들이며 이야기가 시작된다.
aboutEn: A rough young sailor, Martin Eden, steps awkwardly into a well-off family's home, and the story begins there. The opening scene makes you feel his shame and his wish to belong, which makes it a good place to start.

title: 하얀 엄니
author: 잭 런던
opening: Dark spruce forest frowned on either side the frozen waterway. The trees had been stripped by a recent wind of their white covering of frost, and they seemed to lean towards each other, black and ominous, in the fading light. A vast silence reigned over the land.
about: 얼어붙은 북극 황야에서 썰매개 무리와 늑대가 등장하는 야생 모험 소설이다.
aboutEn: This adventure novel opens in the frozen Northland wilderness, with a string of sled dogs and wolves. Its harsh, vivid depiction of the Wild makes you think about how living things survive in it.

title: 소리와 분노
author: 윌리엄 포크너
opening: Through the fence, between the curling flower spaces, I could see them hitting. They were coming toward where the flag was and I went along the fence. Luster was hunting in the grass by the flower tree. They took the flag out, and they were hitting.
about: 서른세 살 남자의 눈에 비친 풍경으로 시작하는, 남부 가족을 다룬 윌리엄 포크너의 소설이다.
aboutEn: William Faulkner's novel about a Southern family opens through the eyes of a thirty-three-year-old man at a fence. Its unusual way of telling the story asks you to piece together what is happening as you read.

title: 율리시스
author: 제임스 조이스
opening: Stately, plump Buck Mulligan came from the stairhead, bearing a bowl of lather on which a mirror and a razor lay crossed. A yellow dressinggown, ungirdled, was sustained gently behind him on the mild morning air. He held the bowl aloft and intoned: —Introibo ad altare Dei.
about: 벅 멀리건이 면도 대접을 들고 탑 계단 위에 나타나는 장면으로 시작하는 조이스의 장편소설이다.
aboutEn: James Joyce's novel opens with Buck Mulligan appearing on a tower stairhead, bearing a bowl of lather. The opening pages show its playful, dense language, and they make it worth reading slowly.

title: 허랜드
author: 샬럿 퍼킨스 길먼
opening: This is written from memory, unfortunately. If I could have brought with me the material I so carefully prepared, this would be a very different story. Whole books full of notes, carefully copied records, firsthand descriptions, and the pictures—that's the worst loss.
about: 세 남자가 여자들만 사는 외딴 나라를 찾아가는 이야기를 한 사람의 기억으로 풀어낸 소설이다.
aboutEn: Three men set out to find a land inhabited only by women, and one of them recounts it from memory. It lets you test your own assumptions about gender and society against what the narrator finds.

title: 마음
author: 나쓰메 소세키
opening: 私はその人を常に先生と呼んでいた。だからここでもただ先生と書くだけで本名は打ち明けない。これは世間を憚かる遠慮というよりも、その方が私にとって自然だからである。私はその人の記憶を呼び起すごとに、すぐ「先生」といいたくなる。筆を執っても心持は同じ事である。よそよそしい頭文字などはとても使う気にならない。 私が先生と知り合いになったのは鎌倉である。その時私はまだ若々しい書生であった。暑中休暇を利用して海水浴に行った友達からぜひ来いという端書を受け取ったので、私は多少の金を工面して、出掛ける事にした。私は金の工面に二、三日を費やした。
about: 가마쿠라 해변에서 '선생님'을 만난 젊은 서생이 그 사람을 회상하는 일본 소설이다.
aboutEn: A young student recalls meeting a man he calls Sensei at the beach in Kamakura. The quiet, restrained narration makes you wonder about the person behind that name and why he is never named.

title: 도련님
author: 나쓰메 소세키
opening: 親譲りの無鉄砲で小供の時から損ばかりしている。小学校に居る時分学校の二階から飛び降りて一週間ほど腰を抜かした事がある。なぜそんな無闇をしたと聞く人があるかも知れぬ。別段深い理由でもない。新築の二階から首を出していたら、同級生の一人が冗談に、いくら威張っても、そこから飛び降りる事は出来まい。弱虫やーい。と囃したからである。小使に負ぶさって帰って来た時、おやじが大きな眼をして二階ぐらいから飛び降りて腰を抜かす奴があるかと云ったから、この次は抜かさずに飛んで見せますと答えた。 親類のものから西洋製のナイフを貰って奇麗な刃を日に翳して、友達に見せていたら、一人が光る事は光るが切れそうもないと云った。
about: 무모한 성격 탓에 어릴 적부터 손해만 보아 온 '나'가 자신의 유년 시절을 회고하며 풀어 가는 이야기다.
aboutEn: A man whose reckless nature has cost him dearly since childhood looks back on his boyhood pranks and his cold family.

title: 라쇼몽
author: 아쿠타가와 류노스케
opening: ある日の暮方の事である。一人の下人が、羅生門の下で雨やみを待っていた。 広い門の下には、この男のほかに誰もいない。ただ、所々丹塗の剥げた、大きな円柱に、蟋蟀が一匹とまっている。羅生門が、朱雀大路にある以上は、この男のほかにも、雨やみをする市女笠や揉烏帽子が、もう二三人はありそうなものである。それが、この男のほかには誰もいない。 何故かと云うと、この二三年、京都には、地震とか辻風とか火事とか饑饉とか云う災がつづいて起った。そこで洛中のさびれ方は一通りではない。旧記によると、仏像や仏具を打砕いて、その丹がついたり、金銀の箔がついたりした木を、路ばたにつみ重ねて、薪の料に売っていたと云う事である。
about: 재난으로 황폐해진 교토, 해고당한 하인 한 사람이 비를 피해 라쇼몽 아래에서 갈 곳을 몰라 서 있는 장면에서 시작한다.
aboutEn: In a Kyoto ruined by disasters, a dismissed servant waits out the rain beneath the Rashomon gate with nowhere to go.

title: 갓파
author: 아쿠타가와 류노스케
opening: これはある精神病院の患者、――第二十三号がだれにでもしゃべる話である。彼はもう三十を越しているであろう。が、一見したところはいかにも若々しい狂人である。彼の半生の経験は、――いや、そんなことはどうでもよい。彼はただじっと両膝をかかえ、時々窓の外へ目をやりながら、（鉄格子をはめた窓の外には枯れ葉さえ見えない樫の木が一本、雪曇りの空に枝を張っていた。）院長のＳ博士や僕を相手に長々とこの話をしゃべりつづけた。もっとも身ぶりはしなかったわけではない。彼はたとえば「驚いた」と言う時には急に顔をのけぞらせたりした。…… 僕はこういう彼の話をかなり正確に写したつもりである。
about: 정신병원 환자 제23호가 자신이 겪은 일이라며 되풀이해 들려주는 이야기이며, 산속에서 갓파를 처음 만난 장면으로 이어진다.
aboutEn: Patient No. 23 of a mental hospital tells of climbing a mountain in dense fog, where he first meets a kappa.

title: 덤불 속
author: 아쿠타가와 류노스케
opening: さようでございます。あの死骸を見つけたのは、わたしに違いございません。わたしは今朝いつもの通り、裏山の杉を伐りに参りました。すると山陰の藪の中に、あの死骸があったのでございます。あった処でございますか？ それは山科の駅路からは、四五町ほど隔たって居りましょう。竹の中に痩せ杉の交った、人気のない所でございます。 死骸は縹の水干に、都風のさび烏帽子をかぶったまま、仰向けに倒れて居りました。何しろ一刀とは申すものの、胸もとの突き傷でございますから、死骸のまわりの竹の落葉は、蘇芳に滲みたようでございます。いえ、血はもう流れては居りません。傷口も乾いて居ったようでございます。
about: 덤불 속에서 발견된 사내의 주검을 두고 관계자들이 관아에서 차례로 증언하는 형식을 취한 단편이다.
aboutEn: A short story in which several witnesses give testimony about a man's body found in a bamboo thicket.

title: 거미줄
author: 아쿠타가와 류노스케
opening: ある日の事でございます。御釈迦様は極楽の蓮池のふちを、独りでぶらぶら御歩きになっていらっしゃいました。池の中に咲いている蓮の花は、みんな玉のようにまっ白で、そのまん中にある金色の蕊からは、何とも云えない好い匂が、絶間なくあたりへ溢れて居ります。極楽は丁度朝なのでございましょう。 やがて御釈迦様はその池のふちに御佇みになって、水の面を蔽っている蓮の葉の間から、ふと下の容子を御覧になりました。この極楽の蓮池の下は、丁度地獄の底に当って居りますから、水晶のような水を透き徹して、三途の河や針の山の景色が、丁度覗き眼鏡を見るように、はっきりと見えるのでございます。
about: 극락 연못가를 거닐던 부처가 지옥 바닥에서 허우적대는 큰 도둑 칸다타를 보고 거미줄을 내려 주는 이야기다.
aboutEn: The Buddha, strolling by a lotus pond in paradise, spots the thief Kandata in the depths of hell and lowers a spider's thread to him.

title: 납함
author: 루쉰
opening: 我在年青時候也曾經做過許多夢，後來大半忘卻了，但自己也並不以為可惜。所謂回憶者，雖說可以使人歡欣，有時也不免使人寂寞，使精神的絲縷還牽着已逝的寂寞的時光，又有什麽意味呢，而我偏苦於不能全忘卻，這不能全忘的一部分，到現在便成了吶喊的來由。 我有四年多，曾經常常，——幾乎是每天，出入於質鋪和藥店裏，年紀可是忘卻了，總之是藥店的櫃臺正和我一樣高，質鋪的是比我高一倍，我從一倍高的櫃臺外送上衣服或首飾去，在侮蔑裏接了錢，再到一樣高的櫃臺上給我久病的父親去買藥。
about: 루쉰이 젊은 날의 꿈과 의학을 버리고 문학으로 향한 내력을 밝히는 서문으로 열리는 첫 소설집이다.
aboutEn: Lu Xun's first story collection opens with a preface on why he gave up medicine for literature and how loneliness shaped him.

title: 셜록 홈즈의 회상록
author: 아서 코난 도일
opening: I was not surprised. Indeed, my only wonder was that he had not already been mixed up in this extraordinary case, which was the one topic of conversation through the length and breadth of England.
about: 왓슨이 기록한 셜록 홈즈의 사건들을 모은 단편집으로, 첫 장면은 경주마 실종과 조련사 살인 사건을 향해 떠나는 아침이다.
aboutEn: This collection of Sherlock Holmes cases recorded by Watson opens with Holmes leaving for Dartmoor over a missing racehorse and its trainer's murder.

title: 셜록 홈즈의 귀환
author: 아서 코난 도일
opening: It was in the spring of the year 1894 that all London was interested, and the fashionable world dismayed, by the murder of the Honourable Ronald Adair under most unusual and inexplicable circumstances.
about: 홈즈의 귀환을 알리는 단편집으로, 첫 이야기는 1894년 런던을 뒤흔든 로널드 에이다어 살인 사건에서 시작한다.
aboutEn: This Holmes collection begins with the 1894 murder of the Honourable Ronald Adair, a case that shook London.

title: 네 사람의 서명
author: 아서 코난 도일
opening: Sherlock Holmes took his bottle from the corner of the mantel-piece and his hypodermic syringe from its neat morocco case. With his long, white, nervous fingers he adjusted the delicate needle, and rolled back his left shirt-cuff.
about: 왓슨이 홈즈와 함께한 또 다른 사건을 기록한 장편으로, 홈즈가 추리를 어떻게 하나의 학문처럼 다루는지 첫 장부터 보여 준다.
aboutEn: This Sherlock Holmes novel is narrated by Watson, and its first chapter shows Holmes treating deduction almost as a science.

title: 잃어버린 세계
author: 아서 코난 도일
opening: Mr. E. D. Malone desires to state that both the injunction for restraint and the libel action have been withdrawn unreservedly by Professor G. E.
about: 기자 말론이 괴짜 챌린저 교수를 만나 미지의 세계로 향하는 탐험에 나서는 모험 소설이다.
aboutEn: This adventure novel follows the reporter Malone, who meets the formidable Professor Challenger and joins an expedition into the unknown.

title: 에드거 앨런 포 단편선
author: 에드거 앨런 포
match: The Works of Edgar Allan Poe — Volume 2
original: The Works of Edgar Allan Poe, Volume 2
opening: We gave him a hearty welcome; for there was nearly half as much of the entertaining as of the contemptible about the man, and we had not seen him for several years.
about: 에드거 앨런 포의 단편 모음으로, 「어셔가의 몰락」 「함정과 진자」 「아몬티야도 술통」 등이 실려 있다.
aboutEn: This volume of Edgar Allan Poe's tales includes The Fall of the House of Usher, The Pit and the Pendulum and The Cask of Amontillado.

title: 투명인간
author: H. G. 웰스
match: The Invisible Man: A Grotesque Romance
opening: The stranger came early in February, one wintry day, through a biting wind and a driving snow, the last snowfall of the year, over the down, walking from Bramblehurst railway station, and carrying a little black portmanteau in his thickly gloved hand.
about: 어느 겨울날 온몸을 붕대와 옷으로 감싼 낯선 사내가 시골 마을 아이핑의 여관에 나타나면서 시작되는 H. G. 웰스의 소설이다. 정체를 숨긴 사내를 둘러싼 마을 사람들의 의심과 소동을 따라가게 된다.
aboutEn: H. G. Wells's novel begins when a stranger, wrapped from head to foot, arrives at the Coach and Horses inn in a snowstorm.

title: 지구 속 여행
author: 쥘 베른
match: A Journey to the Centre of the Earth
original: A Journey to the Centre of the Earth
opening: Looking back to all that has occurred to me since that eventful day, I am scarcely able to believe in the reality of my adventures. They were truly so wonderful that even now I am bewildered when I think of them. My uncle was a German, having married my mother's sister, an Englishwoman.
about: 쥘 베른이 쓴 모험 소설로, 조카의 시점에서 삼촌이 어떤 대발견을 하며 지구 속 여행이 시작되는 과정을 따라간다.
aboutEn: Jules Verne's adventure is told by a nephew, and it begins with his uncle's great discovery that launches a journey into the earth.

title: 크툴루의 부름
author: H. P. 러브크래프트
opening: "Of such great powers or beings there may be conceivably a survival ... a survival of a hugely remote period when ... consciousness was manifested, perhaps, in shapes and forms long since withdrawn before the tide of advancing humanity ...
about: 한 화자가 죽은 사람의 수기와 낡은 신문 기사를 맞추어 보다가 인류가 알아서는 안 될 태곳적 존재의 흔적에 다가가는 러브크래프트의 단편이다.
aboutEn: A narrator pieces together a dead man's notes and an old newspaper item, and edges toward traces of an ancient being humanity was never meant to know, in this Lovecraft tale from Weird Tales, 1928.

title: 사람은 무엇으로 사는가
author: 레프 톨스토이
match: What Men Live By, and Other Tales
original: What Men Live By, and Other Tales
opening: A shoemaker named Simon, who had neither house nor land of his own, lived with his wife and children in a peasant's hut, and earned his living by his work. Work was cheap, but bread was dear, and what he earned he spent for food.
about: 구두장이 시몬 이야기와 '사람에게는 땅이 얼마나 필요한가' 등을 담은 톨스토이의 단편집으로, 첫머리에 사랑을 말하는 요한의 편지 구절이 놓여 있다.
aboutEn: This Tolstoy collection includes the tale of the shoemaker Simon and 'How Much Land Does a Man Need?', opening with verses on love from the Epistle of John.

title: 오디세이아
author: 호메로스
match: The Odyssey / Rendered into English prose for the use of those who cannot read the original
opening: This translation is intended to supplement a work entitled "The Authoress of the Odyssey", which I published in 1897. I could not give the whole "Odyssey" in that book without making it unwieldy, I therefore epitomised my translation, which was already completed and which I now publish in full.
about: 호메로스의 서사시를 영어 산문으로 옮긴 번역본으로, 서문에서 번역자 새뮤얼 버틀러가 작품의 배경에 대한 자신의 주장을 밝힌다.
aboutEn: An English prose translation of Homer's epic, whose preface lays out the translator's own theory about where and by whom the poem was written.

title: 일리아스
author: 호메로스
opening: The quarrel between Agamemnon and Achilles—Achilles withdraws from the war, and sends his mother Thetis to ask Jove to help the Trojans—Scene between Jove and Juno on Olympus. Sing, O goddess, the anger of Achilles son of Peleus, that brought countless ills upon the Achaeans.
about: 트로이아 전쟁 중 아가멤논과 아킬레우스가 다투는 데서 시작하는 호메로스의 서사시를 영어 산문으로 옮긴 번역본이다.
aboutEn: An English prose translation of Homer's epic, which begins with the quarrel between Agamemnon and Achilles during the Trojan War.

title: 신곡
author: 단테 알리기에리
opening: In the midway of this our mortal life, / I found me in a gloomy wood, astray / Gone from the path direct: and e'en to tell / It were no easy task, how savage wild / That forest, how robust and rough its growth, / Which to remember only, my dismay
about: 서른five 살의 시인이 어두운 숲에서 길을 잃고 표범을 마주치는 장면으로 시작하는 단테의 서사시다. 인간의 삶과 두려움을 여행의 틀로 풀어내는 방식을 따라가 볼 만하다.
aboutEn: Dante's epic poem opens with a poet lost in a dark wood who meets a panther on a lonely slope. Its way of framing fear and the course of a human life as a journey gives readers a lot to think about.

title: 풀잎
author: 월트 휘트먼
opening: Come, said my soul, / Such verses for my Body let us write, (for we are one,) / That should I after return, / Or, long, long hence, in other spheres, / There to some group of mates the chants resuming, / (Tallying Earth's soil, trees, winds, tumultuous waves,)
about: 월트 휘트먼이 몸과 영혼, 미국과 사랑을 노래한 시를 묶은 시집이다. 자유로운 호흡의 시구가 몸과 자아를 어떻게 긍정하는지 살펴볼 수 있다.
aboutEn: Walt Whitman's verse collection sings of the body, the soul, America and love. Its free-flowing lines show how a poet can affirm the self and the body.

title: 님의 침묵
author: 한용운
opening: 푸른산빗을ᄭᅢ치고 단풍나무숩을향하야난 적은길을 거러서 참어ᄯᅥᆯ치고 갓슴니다 黃金의ᄭᅩᆺ가티 굿고빗나든 옛盟誓는 차듸찬ᄯᅴᄭᅳᆯ이되야서 한숨의微風에 나러갓슴니다 날카로은 첫｢키쓰｣의追憶은 나의運命의指針을 돌너노코 뒤ㅅ거름처서 사러젓슴니다 나는 향긔로은 님의말소리에 귀먹고 ᄭᅩᆺ다은 님의얼골에 눈머럿슴니다 사랑도 사람의일이라 맛날ᄯᅢ에 미리 ᄯᅥ날것을 염녀하고경계하지 아니한것은아니지만 리별은 ᄯᅳᆺ밧긔일이되고 놀난가슴은 새로은슯음에 터짐니다 그러나 리별을 쓸데업는 눈물의源泉을만들고 마는것은 스々로 사랑을ᄭᅢ치는것인줄 아는ᄭᅡ닭에 것잡
about: 한용운의 시집으로, 목차에 「님의 침묵」「리별은 美의 創造」「알ㅅ수업서요」 등의 시가 실려 있다. 떠난 님을 향한 마음을 옛 표기의 한국어로 읽어 볼 수 있다.
aboutEn: This is Han Yong-un's poetry collection, with poems such as "Silence of the Beloved" listed in its contents. It lets readers meet a longing for an absent beloved in early modern Korean orthography.

title: 오감도
author: 이상
opening: 싸홈하는사람은즉싸홈하지아니하든사람이고또싸홈하는사람은싸홈하지아니하는사람이엇기도하니까싸홈하는사람이싸홈하는구경을하고십거든싸홈하지아니하든사람이싸홈하는것을구경하든지싸홈하지아니하는사람이싸홈하는구경을하든지싸홈하지아니하든사람이나싸홈하지아니하는사람이싸홈하지아니하는것을구경하든지하얏으면그만이다 烏瞰圖 李霜 3 詩第四號 患者의容態에關한問題.
about: 이상의 연작시로, 열세 명의 아이가 길로 달려가는 장면에서 시작해 숫자와 도형, 수술 같은 낯선 소재를 다룬다. 기존 시의 틀을 벗어난 실험적 표현이 무엇을 말하려는지 따져 볼 만하다.
aboutEn: Yi Sang's serial poem begins with thirteen children and moves on to odd subjects such as numbers, mirrors and surgery. Its experimental form invites readers to ask what a poem can do beyond convention.

title: 정지용 시집
author: 정지용
opening: 우리들의 汽車[기차]는 아지랑이 남실거리는 섬나라 봄날 왼하로를 익살스런 마드로스 파이프로 피우며 간 단 다. 우리들의 汽車[기차]는 느으릿 느으릿 유월소 걸어가듯 걸어 간 단 다. 우리들의 汽車[기차]는 노오란 배추꽃 비탈밭 새로 헐레벌덕어리며 지나 간 단 다. 나는 언제든지 슬프기는 슬프나마 마음만은 가벼워 나는 車窓[차창]에 기댄 대로 희파람이나 날리쟈. 먼데 산이 軍馬[군마]처럼 뛰여오고 가까운데 수풀이 바람처럼 불려 가고 유리판을 펼친듯, 瀨戶內海[뢰호내해] 퍼언한 물 물. 물. 물.
about: 정지용의 초기 시를 모은 시집으로, 기차를 타고 가는 화자의 풍경과 도시의 밤거리가 감각적으로 그려진다. 한자와 새로운 말씨가 어우러진 1920년대 한국어 시의 결을 느낄 수 있다.
aboutEn: This collection of Jeong Ji-yong's early poems pictures a traveler on a train and a city at night in vivid sensory detail. It shows the texture of 1920s Korean verse, mixing Chinese characters with fresh diction.

title: 백록담
author: 정지용
opening: 내가 홀로 속엣소리로 그대의 기거를 문의할삼아도 어찌 홀한 말로 부칠 법도 한 일이 아니오니까. 무슨 말씀으로나 좀더 높일 만한 좀 더 그대께 마땅한 언사가 없으오리까. 눈감고 자는 비둘기보다도, 꽃 그림자 옮기는 겨를에 여미며 자는 꽃봉오리보다도, 어여삐 자시올 그대여! 그대의 눈을 들어 풀이하오리까. 속속들이 맑고 푸른 호수가 한 쌍. 밤은 한 폭 그대의 호수에 깃들이기 위하여 있는 것이오리까. 내가 어찌 감히 금성(金星) 노릇하여 그대 호수에 잠길 법도 한 일이오니까.
about: 정지용의 시집으로, 본문 앞머리에서 화자는 높이 우러르는 그대를 향해 공손한 말투로 말을 건넨다. 조개껍질과 바다 같은 이미지가 외로움을 어떻게 드러내는지 읽어 볼 만하다.
aboutEn: This is a collection by Jeong Ji-yong, whose opening poem addresses a revered "you" in a deferential voice. Its images of shells and the sea show how loneliness can be given form.

title: 진달래꽃
author: 김소월
opening: 내게 두고는 당신때문에 밝은 아침이라고 할 것입니다. 땅이 꺼져도 하늘이 무너져도 내게 두고는 끝까지 모두다 당신때문에 있습니다. 다시는, 나의 이러한 맘뿐은, 때가 되면, 그림자같이 당신한테로 가우리다. 오오, 나의 애인(愛人)이었던 당신이여. 무주공산 꿈 1 닭 개 짐승조차도 꿈이 있다고 이르는 말이야 있지 않은가, 그러하다, 봄날은 꿈꿀 때. 내 몸에야 꿈이나 있으랴, 아아 내 세상의 끝이여, 나는 꿈이 그립어, 꿈이 그립어. 맘 켱기는 날 오실 날 아니 오시는 사람! 오시는 것 같게도 맘 켱기는 날!
about: 김소월의 시집으로, 떠난 사람을 그리는 마음과 봄밤, 달빛 같은 풍경이 담겨 있다. 쉬운 말로 쓰인 이별의 정서가 오래 남는 이유를 생각해 볼 수 있다.
aboutEn: Kim Sowol's collection of poems holds longing for those who have gone, set among spring nights and moonlight. Its plain language lets readers consider why its sense of parting lingers.

title: 하늘과 바람과 별과 시
author: 윤동주
opening: 산모퉁이를 돌아 논가 외딴우물을 홀로 찾어가선 가만히 들여다봅니다. 우물속에는 달이 밝고 구름이 흐르고 하늘이 펼치고 파아란 바람이 불고 가을이 있습니다. 그리고 한 사나이가 있습니다. 어쩐지 그 사나이가 미워저 돌아갑니다. 돌아가다 생각하니 그 사나이가 가엾어집니다. 도로 가 들여다 보니 사나이는 그대로 있습니다. 다시 그 사나이가 미워져 돌아갑니다. 돌아가다 생각하니 그 사나이가 그리워집니다. 우물속에는 달이 밝고 구름이 흐르고 하늘이 펼치고 파아란 바람이 불고 가을이 있고 追憶처럼 사나이가 있습니다.
about: 윤동주의 시집으로, 우물 속에 비친 자신을 바라보는 장면 등 일상의 풍경과 자기 성찰이 이어진다. 조용한 말투 속에서 청춘의 부끄러움과 그리움을 읽을 수 있다.
aboutEn: Yun Dong-ju's collection moves through everyday scenes, such as a man looking at himself in a well, toward quiet self-reflection. Its gentle voice carries a young person's shame and longing.

title: 육사시집
author: 이육사
opening: 밤마다 내 꿈은 서해(西海)를 밀항(密航)하는 「짱크」와 같애 소금에 절고 조수(潮水)에 부프러 올랐다. 항상 흐렸한밤 암초(暗礁)를 벗어나면 태풍(颱風)과 싸워가고 전설(傳說)에 읽어본 산호도(珊瑚島)는 구경도 못하는 그곳은 남십자성(南十字星)이 비쳐주도 않았다. 쫓기는 마음 지친 몸이길래 그리운 지평선(地平線)을 한숨에 기오르면 시궁치는 열대식물(熱帶植物)처럼 발목을 오여쌋다 새벽 밀물에 밀려온 거미이냐 다 삭아빠즌 소라 깍질에 나는 붙어 왔다.
about: 이육사가 황혼, 바다, 사막, 무덤 같은 이미지에 방랑과 상실의 정서를 담아 쓴 시를 묶은 시집이다.
aboutEn:
This collection of Yi Yuksa's poems sets feelings of wandering and loss among images of dusk, sea, desert and grave.
Its dense mix of Korean and Chinese-character vocabulary shows how a poet of his time gave voice to longing.

title: 기탄잘리
author: 라빈드라나트 타고르
opening: Other Indians came to see me and their reverence for this man sounded strange in our world, where we hide great and little things under the same veil of obvious comedy and half-serious depreciation. When we were making the cathedrals had we a like reverence for our great men?
about: 타고르가 벵골어 시를 직접 영어 산문으로 옮긴 노래 시집이며, 예이츠의 서문이 앞에 실려 있다.
aboutEn:
This is Tagore's own English prose rendering of his Bengali devotional songs, introduced by W. B. Yeats.
The introduction shows how a Western poet first met these verses and why they stirred him.

title: 변신 이야기 1
author: 오비디우스
match: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books I-VII
original: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books I-VII
opening: The text is based on two reprints of the 1851 Riley translation: Bell (1893, London) and McKay (1899, Philadelphia). Page and line numbers in the left margin refer to Bell; numbers in the right margin are from McKay.
about: 오비디우스가 그리스·로마 신화를 변신이라는 주제로 엮은 서사시의 1권부터 7권까지를 릴리의 영어 산문 번역으로 옮겼다.
aboutEn:
This volume holds Books I-VII of Ovid's Metamorphoses, a compendium of Greek and Roman myth, in Henry T. Riley's prose translation.
It offers a way into the stories behind much later art and literature, with the translator's introduction to guide the reader.

title: 변신 이야기 2
author: 오비디우스
match: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
original: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
opening: If any of these characters do not display properly, or if the apostrophes and quotation marks in this paragraph appear as garbage, you may have an incompatible browser or unavailable fonts. First, make sure that the browser's "character set" or "file encoding" is set to Unicode (UTF-8).
about: 오비디우스의 『변신 이야기』 8권부터 15권까지를 릴리의 영어 산문 번역으로 실었고, 이야기마다 번역자의 요약이 붙는다.
aboutEn:
This volume carries Books VIII-XV of Ovid's Metamorphoses in Riley's prose translation, with a short synopsis for each fable.
Tales such as Daedalus and Icarus and Orpheus and Eurydice can be read one at a time.

title: 에밀리 디킨슨 시집
author: 에밀리 디킨슨
match: Poems by Emily Dickinson, Series One
original: Poems by Emily Dickinson, Series One
opening: THE verses of Emily Dickinson belong emphatically to what Emerson long since called "the Poetry of the Portfolio,"—something produced absolutely without the thought of publication, and solely by way of expression of the writer's own mind.
about: 에밀리 디킨슨이 생전에 거의 발표하지 않고 써 둔 시를 모은 첫 번째 시집으로, 편집자의 서문이 앞에 놓인다.
aboutEn:
This is the first series of Emily Dickinson's poems, most of them written without thought of publication, with an editor's preface.
The verses show a private mind that held to its own strict standard and ignored convention.

title: 셰익스피어 소네트
author: 윌리엄 셰익스피어
opening: That thereby beauty's rose might never die, / But as the riper should by time decease, / His tender heir might bear his memory: / But thou, contracted to thine own bright eyes, / Feed'st thy light's flame with self-substantial fuel, / Making a famine where abundance lies,
about: 셰익스피어의 소네트를 모은 시집으로, 아름다운 젊은이에게 자식을 남기라고 권하는 시들로 시작한다.
aboutEn:
This collection of Shakespeare's sonnets opens by urging a beautiful young man to have a child and so preserve his beauty.
The fourteen-line form compresses argument and feeling, and the opening poems make an easy place to begin.

title: 순수와 경험의 노래
author: 윌리엄 블레이크
match: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
original: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
opening: Introduction / The Shepherd / The Echoing Green / The Lamb / The Little Black Boy / The Blossom
about: 윌리엄 블레이크가 어린 양과 피리 부는 사람 같은 순수의 세계와 그 반대편의 경험의 세계를 짝지어 노래한 시집이다.
aboutEn:
William Blake's paired collection sets a world of innocence, with its lambs and a piping child, against a world of experience.
Reading the poems side by side invites the reader to compare the two ways of seeing.

title: 루바이야트
author: 오마르 하이얌
opening: Omar Khayyam was born at Naishapur in Khorassan in the latter half of our Eleventh, and died within the First Quarter of our Twelfth Century.
about: 11~12세기 페르시아의 천문학자이자 시인 오마르 하이얌의 사행시를 영어로 옮긴 책이며, 그의 생애를 다룬 글이 앞에 실려 있다.
aboutEn:
This book presents the quatrains of Omar Khayyam, the Persian astronomer-poet of the eleventh and twelfth centuries, in English, preceded by an account of his life.
The opening account of his friendship with two schoolmates adds a human story to the verse.

title: 실낙원
author: 존 밀턴
opening: Of Mans First Disobedience, and the Fruit / Of that Forbidden Tree, whose mortal tast / Brought Death into the World, and all our woe, / With loss of Eden, till one greater Man / Restore us, and regain the blissful Seat, / Sing Heav'nly Muse, that on the secret top
about: 존 밀턴이 인간의 첫 불순종과 낙원의 상실을 무운시로 노래한 영어 서사시다. 시인은 하느님의 섭리를 옹호하겠다고 밝히며 첫머리부터 뮤즈에게 도움을 청한다.
aboutEn: John Milton's English epic poem sings of humanity's first disobedience and the loss of Eden. It opens with an invocation of the Muse and a stated aim to justify the ways of God to men.

title: 백팔번뇌
author: 최남선
opening: 석양(夕陽)의 만월대(滿月臺) 터를웃고 지나가노라. 사람 같은 그림 속에 그림 같은 사람 모여, 공보담 빠른 눈짓 번개처럼 치고맞던, 향진(香塵)을 아니 찾으랴 구정(毬庭) 밟고 가리라. 송악산(松嶽山) 봄 수풀에 갖은 새가 노래하고, '병풍(屛風)에 그린 황계(黃鷄)' 나래 치며 울려건만, '연쌍비(燕雙飛)' 한번 간 넋은 돌아 언제 오는고. 천왕봉에서 인간(人間)에 발부리고 하늘 위에 머리 두어, 아침 해 저녁달을 금은(金銀) 한 쌍 공만 여겨 번갈아 두 편 손끝에 주건 받건 하더라.
about: 최남선이 '님'을 향한 마음을 시조 형식으로 엮은 연작 시조집이다. 짧은 가락마다 기다림과 그리움, 속고 속이는 마음의 움직임이 이어져 읽는 이를 붙든다.
aboutEn: Choe Nam-seon's sijo collection weaves a series of verses addressed to a beloved 'nim'. Each short poem traces longing, waiting and the shifting of the heart, offering a close look at the form.

title: 영랑시선
author: 김영랑
opening: 李도령은 殘忍스레 우섰다 저때문의 貞節이 자랑스러워 「우리집이 팍 亡해서 上거지가 되었지야」 틀림없는 도련님 春香은 원망도 않했니라 오! 一片丹心 모진 春香이 그밤새벽에 또 까무러처서는 영 다시 깨어나진 못했었다 두견은 우렀건만 도련님 다시뵈어 恨을 풀었으나 살아날 가망은 아조 끈끼고 왼몸 푸른 脈도 홱 풀려 버렸을법 出道 끝에 御史는 春香의몸을 거두며 울다 「내 卞哥보다 殘忍無智하여 春香을 죽였구나」 오!
about: 김영랑의 시를 가려 모은 시선집으로, 모란이 지는 봄의 슬픔을 노래한 시가 맨 앞에 실려 있다. 당시 말씨를 살린 섬세한 가락과 바다, 달빛, 죽음의 이미지를 따라 읽을 만하다.
aboutEn: This selection of Kim Yeong-rang's poems opens with the sorrow of a spring when the peonies have fallen. Its delicate rhythms and period spellings, with images of sea, moonlight and death, reward a slow reading.

title: 박용철 시집
author: 박용철
opening: 나는 다만 깊히백인 사랑의 총명함으로 아라볼수 잇느니. 여기 멍에아래 마차 끄으는 추렷한 말은 그시절 봄날빗아래 금잔듸 넓은 마당에서 호─롱소리치며 네굽노코 달리다가 가볍게 잔거름 노튼 그 아름답든 나의사랑하든 망아지 그놈이다. 저의 두눈은 굴러 하날을 처다볼 생각도업시, 저의 네발은 따에서 두자 뛰여오를 기운도업시, 쉴틈업시 내리는 채찍에 몰려다니다가는 목에 여물통을 건대로 배채울것을 먹고잇다. 나는 넘처오르는 가슴과 떨리는 주먹으로 듸려다보며, 눈을 감지도못하고 깁고놉흔 하날로 돌려바리도 못한다.
about: 박용철의 시를 모은 시집으로, 이별과 외로움, 비 오는 날의 그리움을 담은 시가 실려 있다. 항구의 눈보라와 빗소리 같은 장면이 쓸쓸한 정서를 낳는 방식을 살필 수 있다.
aboutEn: This is a collection of Park Yong-cheol's poems on parting, loneliness and longing on rainy days. Scenes like a snowy harbor and falling rain show how he builds a quiet, sorrowful mood.

title: 현해탄
author: 임화
opening: 너도 잘 알고 나도 잘 아는 멀쩡한 사실이 아니냐? 보아라! 어느 누가 참말로 도적놈이냐? 이 눈물나는 가난한 젊은 날이 가진 불쌍한 즐거움을 노리는 마음하고, 그 조그만 참말로 풍선(風船)보다 엷은 숨을 안 깨치려는 간지런 마음하고, 말하여보아라, 이곳에 가득 찬 고마운 젊은이들아! 순이야, 누이야! 근로하는 청년, 용감한 사내의 연인아! 생각해보아라, 오늘은 네 귀중한 청년인 용감한 사내가 젊은 날을 부지런한 일에 보내던 그 여윈 손가락으로 지금은 굳은 벽돌담에다 달력을 그리겠구나! 또 이거 봐라, 어서.
about: 임화의 시집으로, 종로 거리와 일하는 청년, 누이동생 순이를 부르는 목소리가 앞부분에 나온다. 흐르는 시간과 미래를 향한 다짐이 한 시대의 열기로 읽혀 생각할 거리를 준다.
aboutEn: This is Im Hwa's poetry collection, opening with a voice calling to his younger sister Sun-i amid the streets of Jongno and working young people. Its vows toward time and the future let readers feel the intensity of an era.

title: 성벽
author: 오장환
opening: 가미(加味)를 모르는 한약(漢藥)처럼 쓰고 틉틉하고나. 여수(旅愁) 여수에 잠겼을 때, 나에게는 쬐그만 희망도 숨어버린다. 요령처럼 흔들리는 슬픈 마음이여! 요지경 속으로 나오는 좁은 세상에 이상스러운 세월들 나는 추억이 무성한 숲속에 섰다. 요지경을 메고 다니는 늙은 장돌뱅이의 고달픈 주막꿈처럼 누덕누덕이 기워진 때묻은 추억, 신뢰할 만한 현실은 어디에 있느냐! 나는 시정배와 같이 현실을 모르며 아는 것처럼 믿고 있었다.
about: 오장환의 시집으로, 기녀와 늙은 선원, 항구 도시의 밤 같은 장면이 한자어 짙은 말씨로 그려진다. 낯선 풍경 속에서 허무와 타락을 바라보는 젊은 시인의 시선을 만날 수 있다.
aboutEn: Oh Jang-hwan's poetry collection paints courtesans, an old sailor and nights in a port city in a heavily Sino-Korean diction. It lets readers meet a young poet's gaze on emptiness and decadence in unfamiliar scenes.

title: 병든 서울
author: 오장환
opening: 이곳에 그냥 기쁨에 취하고, 함성에 목메인 겨레를 ...... 그리고 뒤끓는 환희와 깃발의 꽃바다 속에 무수히 따러가는 이동과 근로하는 이들의 행렬을 ...... 춤추는 깃발이여! 나부끼는 마음이여! 이들을 지키라. 너희들은, 자랑스런 너희들 가슴으로 해방이 주는 노래 속에서 또 하나의 검은 쇠사슬이 움직이려 하는 것을 ... 연합군입성 환영의 노래 몰래 쉬던 숨을 크게 쉬니 가슴이, 가슴이, 자꾸만 커진다 아 동편 바다 왼 끝의 대륙에서 오는 벗이여! 아 반구(半球)의 서편 맨 끝에서 오는 동지여!
about: 오장환의 시집으로, 8월 15일 해방 직후의 서울을 두고 기쁨과 불안을 함께 노래한다. 거리의 함성과 술에 취한 청춘, 새 나라에 대한 바람이 뒤섞여 해방 공간의 분위기를 전한다.
aboutEn: Oh Jang-hwan's poetry collection sings both joy and unease in Seoul just after liberation on August 15. Street cheers, drunken youth and hopes for a new nation blend to convey the mood of that moment.

title: 그날이 오면
author: 심훈
opening: 오늘 아침에 차입해 주신 고의적삼을 받고서야 제가 이 곳에 와 있는 것을 집에서도 아신 줄 알았습니다. 잠시도 어머니의 곁을 떠나지 않던 막내둥이의 생사를 한 달 동안이나 아득히 아실 길 없으셨으니 그 동안에 오죽이나 애를 태우셨겠습니까? 그러하오나 저는 이 곳까지 굴러 오는 동안에 꿈에도 생각지 못하던 고생을 겪었건만 그래도 몸 성히 배포 유하게 큰집에 와서 지냅니다.
about: 심훈의 작품집으로, 앞부분에는 감옥에 갇힌 아들이 어머니께 쓴 편지가 실려 있다. 좁은 감방의 고생을 담담히 전하며 어머니를 안심시키는 말투에서 갇힌 이들의 마음가짐을 엿볼 수 있다.
aboutEn: This Shim Hun collection begins with a letter from a son in prison to his mother. Its calm account of cramped cell life and its words of reassurance offer a glimpse into the resolve of those held there.

title: 햄릿
author: 윌리엄 셰익스피어
opening: How say you by that? [Aside.] Still harping on my daughter. Yet he knew me not at first; he said I was a fishmonger. He is far gone, far gone. And truly in my youth I suffered much extremity for love; very near this. I'll speak to him again.—What do you read, my lord? HAMLET. Words, words, words.
about: 망설임과 의심 속에서 한 사람이 어떻게 행동에 이르는지 따라가며 복수와 양심의 무게를 생각해 보게 된다.
aboutEn: Follow one man's doubt and hesitation on the road to action, and consider the weight of revenge and conscience.

title: 맥베스
author: 윌리엄 셰익스피어
opening: "They met me in the day of success; and I have learned by the perfect'st report they have more in them than mortal knowledge. When I burned in desire to question them further, they made themselves air, into which they vanished.
about: 스코틀랜드 왕 덩컨 치하에서 장군 맥베스와 뱅쿠오, 귀족 맥더프 등이 등장하는 셰익스피어의 비극이다.
aboutEn: Shakespeare's tragedy set in Scotland under King Duncan, with the generals Macbeth and Banquo and the nobleman Macduff among its characters.

title: 로미오와 줄리엣
author: 윌리엄 셰익스피어
opening: True, and therefore women, being the weaker vessels, are ever thrust to the wall: therefore I will push Montague's men from the wall, and thrust his maids to the wall. GREGORY. The quarrel is between our masters and us their men. SAMPSON.
about: 베로나에서 대립하는 몬태규 가와 캐풀렛 가를 배경으로 로미오와 줄리엣을 그린 셰익스피어의 희곡이다.
aboutEn: Shakespeare's play set in Verona, where the feuding houses of Montague and Capulet frame the story of Romeo and Juliet.

title: 인형의 집
author: 헨리크 입센
opening: A bell rings in the hall; shortly afterwards the door is heard to open. Enter NORA, humming a tune and in high spirits. She is in outdoor dress and carries a number of parcels; these she lays on the table to the right.
about: 크리스마스 트리를 사 들고 들뜬 모습으로 집에 들어서는 노라의 모습으로 막이 오르는 입센의 희곡이다.
aboutEn: Ibsen's play opens as Nora, in high spirits, comes home laden with parcels and a Christmas tree, inside the Helmers' comfortable house.

title: 진지함의 중요성
author: 오스카 와일드
match: The Importance of Being Earnest: A Trivial Comedy for Serious People
opening: Morning-room in Algernon's flat in Half-Moon Street. The room is luxuriously and artistically furnished. The sound of a piano is heard in the adjoining room. [Lane is arranging afternoon tea on the table, and after the music has ceased, Algernon enters.] ALGERNON.
about: 런던 앨저넌의 아파트에서 오이 샌드위치와 하인 레인의 대사로 시작하는 와일드의 희극으로, 부제는 '진지한 사람들을 위한 사소한 희극'이다.
aboutEn: Wilde's comedy begins in Algernon's London flat with cucumber sandwiches and his servant Lane, and is subtitled 'A Trivial Comedy for Serious People'.

title: 파우스트
author: 요한 볼프강 폰 괴테
match: Faust [part 1]. Translated Into English in the Original Metres
opening: The value of form, in a poetical work, is the first question to be considered. No poet ever understood this question more thoroughly than Goethe himself, or expressed a more positive opinion in regard to it. The alternative modes of translation which he presents (reported by Riemer, quoted by Mrs.
about: 괴테의 『파우스트』를 원작의 운율 그대로 옮긴 영어 번역본으로, 극장의 서막과 서재 장면, 그레트헨 비극 등이 실려 있다.
aboutEn: An English translation of Goethe's Faust in the original metres, with the Prelude at the Theatre, the study scenes and Margaret's story, along with a translator's preface on the task.

title: 오이디푸스 왕 · 안티고네
author: 소포클레스
match: Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
original: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
opening: To Laius, King of Thebes, an oracle foretold that the child born to him by his queen Jocasta would slay his father and wed his mother. So when in time a son was born the infant's feet were riveted together and he was left to die on Mount Cithaeron.
about: 테바이의 왕 라이오스에게 내려진 신탁에서 출발하는 소포클레스의 비극 모음으로, 오이디푸스 왕과 콜로노스의 오이디푸스, 안티고네를 담았다.
aboutEn: Sophocles' Theban plays, Oedipus the King, Oedipus at Colonus and Antigone, begin from the oracle given to Laius, King of Thebes.

title: 리어 왕
author: 윌리엄 셰익스피어
opening: It did always seem so to us; but now, in the division of the kingdom, it appears not which of the Dukes he values most, for qualities are so weighed that curiosity in neither can make choice of either's moiety. KENT. Is not this your son, my lord? GLOUCESTER.
about: 브리튼의 늙은 왕 리어와 세 딸 고너릴, 리건, 코딜리어, 글로스터 백작 가문을 둘러싼 셰익스피어의 비극이다. 권력과 애정, 가족 사이의 신뢰가 어떻게 시험받는지 따라가 볼 만하다.
aboutEn: This Shakespeare tragedy centers on Lear, the aging King of Britain, his three daughters Goneril, Regan and Cordelia, and the household of the Earl of Gloucester. It invites readers to watch how power, love and family trust are put to the test.

title: 오셀로
author: 윌리엄 셰익스피어
opening: Zounds, sir, you are one of those that will not serve God if the devil bid you. Because we come to do you service, and you think we are ruffians, you'll have your daughter cover'd with a Barbary horse; you'll have your nephews neigh to you; you'll have coursers for cousins and gennets for germans.
about: 베네치아에서 키프로스로 무대를 옮겨 가며, 무어인 장군 오셀로와 그의 부관 및 기수 이아고를 둘러싼 이야기를 다룬 셰익스피어의 비극이다.
aboutEn: This Shakespeare tragedy moves from Venice to Cyprus, following the Moorish general Othello and the men around him, including his lieutenant and his ensign Iago.  Its opening scene, in which Roderigo accuses Iago over a grievance about the lieutenancy, invites you to ask whom a person can trust.

title: 한여름 밤의 꿈
author: 윌리엄 셰익스피어
opening: Here is the scroll of every man's name, which is thought fit through all Athens, to play in our interlude before the Duke and Duchess, on his wedding-day at night. BOTTOM. First, good Peter Quince, say what the play treats on; then read the names of the actors; and so grow to a point. QUINCE.
about: 아테네 공작 테세우스의 결혼을 앞두고, 숲속에서 연인들과 요정들과 직공들의 이야기가 얽히는 셰익스피어의 희극이다.
aboutEn: Set in Athens and a nearby wood, this Shakespeare comedy begins as Duke Theseus awaits his wedding and weaves together lovers, fairies and a troupe of tradesmen.  Its mix of court, forest and the clowns' play-within-a-play shows how love can make people see things oddly.

title: 갈매기
author: 안톤 체호프
opening: The scene is laid in the park on SORIN'S estate. A broad avenue of trees leads away from the audience toward a lake which lies lost in the depths of the park.
about: 소린의 영지를 배경으로 배우 아르카디나와 그녀의 아들, 작가 트리고린, 젊은 처녀 니나 등이 얽히는 체호프의 4막 희곡이다.
aboutEn: This four-act play by Chekhov is set on Sorin's country estate and gathers an actress, her son, a writer and a young girl named Nina.  Its opening, with a homemade stage by the lake and characters already weary of their lives, makes you consider what people want from love and art.

title: 벚꽃 동산 외
author: 안톤 체호프
match: Plays by Anton Chekhov, Second Series
opening: It is not the business of a translator to attempt to outdo all others in singing the praises of his raw material. This is a dangerous process and may well lead, as it led Mr. Calderon, to drawing the reader's attention to points of beauty not to be found in the original.
about: 체호프 희곡 선집 두 번째 권으로, 「벚꽃 동산」을 비롯한 작품들과 번역자의 해설이 함께 실려 있다.
aboutEn: This is the second collection of Chekhov's plays in English, including The Cherry Orchard, along with a translator's introduction.  The introduction's notes on Chekhov's early play and on the Russian censor offer a look at how his drama came to be written and read.

title: 피그말리온
author: 조지 버나드 쇼
opening: As will be seen later on, Pygmalion needs, not a preface, but a sequel, which I have supplied in its due place. The English have no respect for their language, and will not teach their children to speak it. They spell it so abominably that no man can teach himself what it sounds like.
about: 음성학 교수가 등장하는 조지 버나드 쇼의 희곡으로, 영어와 말씨를 다룬 저자의 서문이 앞에 붙어 있다.
aboutEn: This George Bernard Shaw play features a professor of phonetics and opens with the author's preface on the English language and how it is spoken.  Shaw's argument that speech marks people out invites you to look at how accent and class are connected.

title: 뜻대로 하세요
author: 윌리엄 셰익스피어
opening: The answer is that they MAY have packed "liue" into a cliche at a time when they were out of "v"'s. . .possibly having used "vv" in place of some "w"'s, etc.
about: 셰익스피어의 희극 「뜻대로 하세요」를 담은 전자책으로, 앞머리에 옛 철자와 인쇄 관행에 대한 편집자의 설명이 있다.
aboutEn: This edition of Shakespeare's comedy As You Like It begins with an editor's note on the spelling and printing habits of the early texts.  The note shows how much a play's printed text can differ from what its author wrote.

title: 템페스트
author: 윌리엄 셰익스피어
opening: The answer is that they MAY have packed "liue" into a cliche at a time when they were out of "v"'s. . .possibly having used "vv" in place of some "w"'s, etc.
about: 셰익스피어의 희곡 「템페스트」를 담은 전자책으로, 앞머리에 옛 철자와 인쇄 관행에 대한 편집자의 설명이 있다.
aboutEn: This edition of Shakespeare's play The Tempest begins with an editor's note on the spelling and printing habits of the early texts.  The note shows how the form of a play's printed text came about.

title: 헤다 가블러
author: 헨리크 입센
opening: From Munich, on June 29, 1890, Ibsen wrote to the Swedish poet, Count Carl Soilsky: "Our intention has all along been to spend the summer in the Tyrol again. But circumstances are against our doing so.
about: 입센이 1890년에 쓴 희곡 「헤다 가블러」로, 서문에는 작품을 쓰던 시기 그가 남긴 편지가 인용되어 있다.
aboutEn: This is Ibsen's play Hedda Gabler, written in 1890, and its introduction quotes letters he wrote while working on it.  Ibsen says he meant to portray Hedda as her father's daughter and to depict human beings rather than problems, which gives you a way into the play.

title: 민중의 적
author: 헨리크 입센
opening: (SCENE.—DR. STOCKMANN'S sitting-room. It is evening. The room is plainly but neatly appointed and furnished. In the right-hand wall are two doors; the farther leads out to the hall, the nearer to the doctor's study.
about: 노르웨이 남부 해안 마을의 온천 담당 의사 스토크만 박사와 시장인 그의 형을 중심으로 한 희곡이다.
aboutEn: This play centers on Dr. Stockmann, medical officer of the baths in a southern Norwegian coastal town, and his brother, the mayor. Its cast of family, editors and townspeople gathered at a public meeting invites you to ask what happens when one person's duty collides with a community's interests.

title: 메데이아
author: 에우리피데스
opening: The Medea, in spite of its background of wonder and enchantment, is not a romantic play but a tragedy of character and situation. It deals, so to speak, not with the romance itself, but with the end of the romance, a thing which is so terribly often the reverse of romantic.
about: 에우리피데스가 이아손과 메데이아의 이야기에서 사랑이 끝난 뒤의 모습을 그린 그리스 비극이다.
aboutEn: This Greek tragedy by Euripides treats the story of Jason and Medea at the point where their romance has ended. Gilbert Murray's rhyming-verse translation and notes show a play of character and situation rather than a tale of enchantment.

title: 타르튀프
author: 몰리에르
opening: Jean Baptiste Poquelin, better known by his stage name of Moliere, stands without a rival at the head of French comedy. Born at Paris in January, 1622, where his father held a position in the royal household, he was educated at the Jesuit College de Clermont, and for some time studied law, which he
about: 몰리에르가 위선자를 주인공으로 삼아 쓴 프랑스 희극으로, 『위선자』라는 이름으로도 알려져 있다.
aboutEn: This French comedy by Molière takes a hypocrite as its title character and is also known as The Hypocrite. It shows the satire of manners and vices that made Molière the leading figure of French comedy.

title: 월든
author: 헨리 데이비드 소로
match: Walden, and On The Duty Of Civil Disobedience
opening: When I wrote the following pages, or rather the bulk of them, I lived alone, in the woods, a mile from any neighbor, in a house which I had built myself, on the shore of Walden Pond, in Concord, Massachusetts, and earned my living by the labor of my hands only.
about: 소로가 매사추세츠 콩코드의 월든 호숫가에 직접 지은 집에서 홀로 2년 2개월을 산 기록이다.
aboutEn: Thoreau records the two years and two months he lived alone in a house he built himself on Walden Pond in Concord, Massachusetts. He writes in the first person and answers plainly what neighbors asked about his food, loneliness and money.

title: 에머슨 수필집
author: 랠프 월도 에머슨
opening: There is one mind common to all individual men. Every man is an inlet to the same and to all of the same. He that is once admitted to the right of reason is made a freeman of the whole estate.
about: 에머슨의 『수필집 제1집』으로, 모든 사람에게 공통된 하나의 정신이 있다는 생각을 역사론에서 펼친다.
aboutEn: This is Emerson's Essays: First Series, which opens with the idea of one mind common to all people. It reads history as the record of that mind and asks you to see your own experience as a key to the past.

title: 예언자
author: 칼릴 지브란
opening: "His power came from some great reservoir of spiritual life else it could not have been so universal and so potent, but the majesty and beauty of the language with which he clothed it were all his own?" —Claude Bragdon THE BOOKS OF KAHLIL GIBRAN The Madman. 1918 Twenty Drawings.
about: 12년을 기다린 배가 오르팔레세 도시에 닿자 예언자 알무스타파가 떠날 채비를 하는 산문시집이다.
aboutEn: This book of prose poems begins as Almustafa, after twelve years in the city of Orphalese, sees his ship come to carry him home. Its short chapters on topics such as eating, buying and selling, and crime and punishment give you a way to reflect on everyday life.

title: 프레더릭 더글러스 자서전
author: 프레더릭 더글러스
match: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave
original: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass
opening: In the month of August, 1841, I attended an anti-slavery convention in Nantucket, at which it was my happiness to become acquainted with Frederick Douglass, the writer of the following Narrative.
about: 노예 신분에서 탈출한 프레더릭 더글러스가 자신의 삶을 직접 적은 1840년대의 자서전이다.
aboutEn: This is the 1840s autobiography in which Frederick Douglass, who escaped from slavery, tells his own life story. An introductory letter from Wendell Phillips shows how abolitionists received his account, and the account itself comes from a man who lived under slavery.

title: 프랭클린 자서전
author: 벤저민 프랭클린
opening: "He was therefore, feasted and invited to all the court parties. At these he sometimes met the old Duchess of Bourbon, who, being a chess player of about his force, they very generally played together. Happening once to put her king into prize, the Doctor took it.
about: 벤저민 프랭클린이 보스턴의 가문과 어린 시절부터 인쇄공 생활, 공직 활동까지 돌아본 자서전이다.
aboutEn: Benjamin Franklin looks back on his life, from his Boston ancestry and boyhood through his years as a printer to his public service. Chapters such as his plan for attaining moral perfection and his scientific experiments let you follow how he tried to improve himself.

title: 권태
author: 이상
opening: 어서, 차라리 어두워버리기나 했으면 좋겠는데─벽촌의 여름날은 지리해서 죽겠을 만치 길다. 동에 팔봉산. 곡선은 왜 저리도 굴곡이 없이 단조로운고? 서를 보아도 벌판, 남을 보아도 벌판, 북을 보아도 벌판, 아─이 벌판은 어쩌라고 이렇게 한이 없이 늘어 놓였을꼬? 어쩌자고 저렇게까지 똑같이 초록색 하나로 돼먹었노? 농가가 가운데 길 하나를 두고 좌우로 한 십여 호씩 있다. 휘청거린 소나무 기둥, 흙을 주물러 바른 벽, 강낭대로 둘러싼 울타리, 울타리를 덮은 호박넝쿨, 모두가 그게 그것같이 똑같다.
about: 벽촌의 여름날, 할 일 없는 화자가 장기를 두고 개울가를 거닐며 끝없는 권태를 마주하는 이상의 수필이다.
aboutEn: In this essay by Yi Sang, a narrator in a remote village spends a long summer day playing janggi and wandering, facing endless boredom.

title: 수상록
author: 미셸 드 몽테뉴
match: Essays of Michel de Montaigne — Complete
opening: Of all egotists, Montaigne, if not the greatest, was the most fascinating, because, perhaps, he was the least affected and most truthful.
about: 몽테뉴가 슬픔, 거짓말, 두려움, 상상력 같은 주제를 두고 쓴 글과 편지를 모은 책이다.
aboutEn: This collection gathers Montaigne's essays and letters on subjects such as sorrow, lying, fear, and the force of imagination.

title: 헬렌 켈러 자서전
author: 헬렌 켈러
match: The Story of My Life / With her letters (1887-1901) and a supplementary account of her education, including passages from the reports and letters of her teacher, Anne Mansfield Sullivan, by John Albert Macy
opening: The Editor desires to express his gratitude and the gratitude of Miss Keller and Miss Sullivan to The Ladies' Home Journal and to its editors, Mr. Edward Bok and Mr. William V.
about: 헬렌 켈러가 직접 쓴 삶의 이야기에 편지와 스승 설리번의 기록, 편집자의 보충 설명을 더한 책이다.
aboutEn: Helen Keller tells her own life story here, joined by her letters, her teacher Anne Sullivan's reports, and an editor's supplementary account.

title: 루소 고백록
author: 장 자크 루소
match: The Confessions of Jean Jacques Rousseau — Complete
original: The Confessions of Jean Jacques Rousseau
opening: Among the notable books of later times—we may say, without exaggeration, of all time—must be reckoned The Confessions of Jean Jacques Rousseau.
about: 루소가 자신의 삶을 스스로 그려 낸 자전적 기록으로, 절대왕정과 봉건제가 저물던 시대를 배경으로 한다.
aboutEn: Rousseau paints his own life in this autobiographical work, set in an age when absolutism and feudalism were making their last stand.

title: 산촌여정
author: 이상
match: 산촌여정(山村餘情) — 성천 기행 중의 몇 절
opening: 향기로운 MJB의 미각을 잊어버린 지도 20여 일이나 됩니다. 이 곳에는 신문도 잘 아니 오고 체전부(遞傳夫)는 이따금 하드롱 빛 소식을 가져옵니다. 거기는 누에고치와 옥수수의 사연이 적혀 있습니다. 마을 사람들은 멀리 떨어져 사는 일가 때문에 수심이 생겼나 봅니다. 나도 도회에 남기고 온 일이 걱정이 됩니다. 건너편 팔봉산에는 노루와 멧돼지가 있답니다. 그리고 기우제 지내던 개골창까지 내려와서 가재를 잡아먹는 곰을 본 사람도 있습니다.
about: 이상이 산골 마을에 머물며 석유 등잔, 별빛, 벌레 소리 같은 풍경을 도회의 기억과 겹쳐 적은 글이다.
aboutEn: Yi Sang writes from a mountain village, setting oil lamps, starlight, and insect sounds against memories of the city.

title: 차의 책
author: 오카쿠라 가쿠조
opening: Tea began as a medicine and grew into a beverage. In China, in the eighth century, it entered the realm of poetry as one of the polite amusements. The fifteenth century saw Japan ennoble it into a religion of aestheticism—Teaism.
about: 오카쿠라 가쿠조가 차를 약에서 음료로, 다시 미를 숭배하는 일본의 다도로 이어진 문화로 풀어낸 책이다.
aboutEn: Okakura Kakuzo traces tea from medicine to beverage to Japan's Teaism, a cult built on the adoration of beauty.

title: 베이컨 수필집
author: 프랜시스 베이컨
match: The Essays or Counsels, Civil and Moral
original: The Essays or Counsels, Civil and Moral
opening: SALOMON saies; A good Name is as a precious oyntment; And I assure my selfe, such wil your Graces Name bee, with Posteritie. For your Fortune, and Merit both, have been Eminent. And you have planted Things, that are like to last.
about: 프랜시스 베이컨이 결혼과 독신, 부모와 자식, 친구, 건강 같은 삶의 문제를 짧은 글로 다룬 수필집이다.
aboutEn: Francis Bacon's essays treat matters such as marriage, parents and children, friends, and health in short, compact pieces.

title: 노예의 굴레를 벗고
author: 부커 T. 워싱턴
opening: I have tried to tell a simple, straightforward story, with no attempt at embellishment. My regret is that what I have attempted to do has been done so imperfectly.
about: 부커 T. 워싱턴이 노예로 태어난 어린 시절부터 교육을 받고 터스키기 학교를 세우기까지의 삶을 쓴 자서전이다.
aboutEn: Booker T. Washington's autobiography follows his life from birth into slavery through his education and his work at Tuskegee.

title: 첼리니 자서전
author: 벤베누토 첼리니
opening: AMONG the vast number of men who have thought fit to write down the history of their own lives, three or four have achieved masterpieces which stand out preeminently: Saint Augustine in his "Confessions," Samuel Pepys in his "Diary," Rousseau in his "Confessions." It is among these extraordinary doc
about: 16세기 이탈리아의 금세공사이자 조각가 벤베누토 첼리니가 자기 삶을 직접 적어 내려간 자서전이다.
aboutEn: This is the autobiography of Benvenuto Cellini, the sixteenth-century Italian goldsmith and sculptor, who tells his own life story.

title: 어느 영국인 아편 중독자의 고백
author: 토머스 드 퀸시
opening: Guilt and misery shrink, by a natural instinct, from public notice: they court privacy and solitude: and even in their choice of a grave will sometimes sequester themselves from the general population of the churchyard, as if declining to claim fellowship with the great family of man, and wishing (i
about: 토머스 드 퀸시가 아편에 빠져 지낸 한 시기를 독자에게 직접 털어놓는 고백록이다.
aboutEn: Thomas De Quincey sets down for the reader the record of a period of his life spent under the spell of opium.

title: 미시시피강의 생활
author: 마크 트웨인
opening: THE Mississippi is well worth reading about. It is not a commonplace river, but on the contrary is in all ways remarkable. Considering the Missouri its main branch, it is the longest river in the world—four thousand three hundred miles.
about: 마크 트웨인이 미시시피강의 역사와 증기선 시절의 경험을 풀어 쓴 책이다.
aboutEn: Mark Twain writes about the history of the Mississippi and his own experiences in the days of steamboats on the river.

title: 당나귀와 떠난 여행
author: 로버트 루이스 스티븐슨
match: Travels with a donkey in the Cevennes
original: Travels with a Donkey in the Cevennes
opening: The journey which this little book is to describe was very agreeable and fortunate for me. After an uncouth beginning, I had the best of luck to the end.
about: 스티븐슨이 프랑스 세벤 지방을 짐을 실은 당나귀와 함께 걸은 여행을 적은 기록이다.
aboutEn: Robert Louis Stevenson records his journey on foot through the Cevennes in France with a donkey to carry his pack.

title: 명상록
author: 마르쿠스 아우렐리우스
opening: In 140 Marcus was raised to the consulship, and in 145 his betrothal was consummated by marriage. Two years later Faustina brought him a daughter; and soon after the tribunate and other imperial honours were conferred upon him. Antoninus Pius died in 161, and Marcus assumed the imperial state.
about: 로마 황제 마르쿠스 아우렐리우스가 스토아 철학의 가르침을 바탕으로 자신을 돌아보며 쓴 글을 모은 책이다.
aboutEn: This collection of writings by the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius reflects on himself through the lens of Stoic philosophy.

title: 국가
author: 플라톤
opening: The Republic of Plato is the longest of his works with the exception of the Laws, and is certainly the greatest of them. There are nearer approaches to modern metaphysics in the Philebus and in the Sophist; the Politicus or Statesman is more ideal; the form and institutions of the State are more cle
about: 플라톤이 대화 형식으로 정의와 이상적인 국가의 모습을 탐구하는 철학서이다.
aboutEn: Plato's dialogue examines justice and the shape of an ideal state through conversation.

title: 소크라테스의 변론
author: 플라톤
opening: In what relation the "Apology" of Plato stands to the real defence of Socrates, there are no means of determining. It certainly agrees in tone and character with the description of Xenophon, who says in the "Memorabilia" that Socrates might have been acquitted "if in any moderate degree he would hav
about: 재판정에 선 소크라테스가 자신을 향한 고발에 맞서 펼친 변론을 플라톤이 기록한 글이다.
aboutEn: Plato's account of the speech Socrates gives in court in answer to the charges brought against him.

title: 향연
author: 플라톤
opening: Of all the works of Plato the Symposium is the most perfect in form, and may be truly thought to contain more than any commentator has ever dreamed of; or, as Goethe said of one of his own writings, more than the author himself knew.
about: 아가톤의 연회에서 소크라테스와 여러 사람이 차례로 사랑을 찬미하는 연설을 하는 플라톤의 대화편이다.
aboutEn: Plato's dialogue in which Socrates and others take turns delivering speeches in praise of love at Agathon's banquet.

title: 니코마코스 윤리학
author: 아리스토텔레스
opening: The principle of distribution of the subject-matter between the two works is far from obvious, and has been much debated. Not much can be gathered from their titles, which in any case were not given to them by their author.
about: 아리스토텔레스가 인간의 행위와 성품을 다룬 윤리학 논고로, 『정치학』과 짝을 이루는 정치학의 한 부분이다. 행복과 덕이 무엇인지 묻는 질문이 오늘의 삶에도 이어지는지 따라가 볼 만하다.
aboutEn: Aristotle's treatise on human conduct and character, the companion half of his Politics within a single political science. It lets you test his questions about happiness and virtue against your own life.

title: 시학
author: 아리스토텔레스
opening: I propose to treat of Poetry in itself and of its various kinds, noting the essential quality of each; to inquire into the structure of the plot as requisite to a good poem; into the number and nature of the parts of which a poem is composed; and similarly into whatever else falls within the same in
about: 아리스토텔레스가 시의 종류와 구조, 특히 비극과 서사시를 모방의 관점에서 논한 글로, 부처(Butcher)의 번역이다. 줄거리 구성이 왜 중요한지 따져 보는 논의가 지금의 이야기 읽기에도 쓸모가 있다.
aboutEn: Aristotle's inquiry into poetry and its kinds, especially tragedy and epic, treated as modes of imitation, in S. H. Butcher's translation. His argument about why plot structure matters still sharpens how we read stories.

title: 엥케이리디온
author: 에픽테토스
opening: That there was a rebirth of Stoicism in the centuries of rebirth which marked the emergence of the modern age was not mere chance. Philosophical, moral, and social conditions of the time united to cause it.
about: 에픽테토스의 가르침을 엮은 짧은 스토아 철학 안내서로, '手冊'이라는 뜻의 제목을 지닌다. 우리가 통제할 수 있는 것과 없는 것을 가르는 태도를 몇 쪽 안에서 곱씹게 한다.
aboutEn: A short Stoic manual drawn from the teaching of Epictetus, whose title means "handbook." In a few pages it invites you to rethink what lies within your control and what does not.

title: 고백록
author: 아우구스티누스
opening: And how shall I call upon my God, my God and Lord, since, when I call for Him, I shall be calling Him to myself? and what room is there within me, whither my God can come into me? whither can God come into me, God who made heaven and earth?
about: 아우구스티누스가 하느님께 직접 말을 건네는 형식으로 쓴 신앙과 자기 성찰의 기록이다. "우리 마음은 당신 안에서 쉬기까지 평안하지 못하다"는 첫머리의 물음이 이 책을 읽어 나갈 실마리가 된다.
aboutEn: Augustine's work of faith and self-examination, written as a prayer addressed directly to God. Its opening claim that the heart is restless until it rests in God gives a thread to follow through the book.

title: 손자병법
author: 손무
opening: When Lionel Giles began his translation of Sun Tzŭ's Art of War, the work was virtually unknown in Europe. Its introduction to Europe began in 1782 when a French Jesuit Father living in China, Joseph Amiot, acquired a copy of it, and translated it into French.
about: 손무가 전쟁의 계획과 운용, 책략, 첩보 등을 열세 편으로 풀어낸 고대 중국의 병서로, 라이오넬 자일스의 영역본이다. 약 2400년 전 글이 지금도 전략을 생각하는 데 쓸모가 있는지 확인해 볼 수 있다.
aboutEn: An ancient Chinese treatise by Sun Tzu on planning, waging war, stratagem and spies, in Lionel Giles's translation. It lets you judge whether a work some 2,400 years old still has lessons for strategy today.

title: 도덕경
author: 노자
match: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics
opening: Ch. 1. 1. The Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao. The name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name. 2. (Conceived of as) having no name, it is the Originator of heaven and earth; (conceived of as) having a name, it is the Mother of all things. 3.
about: 노자의 것으로 전하는 짧은 장들의 모음으로, 말로 이를 수 있는 도는 변치 않는 도가 아니라는 구절로 시작한다. 이름과 대립, 함이 없는 다스림을 다루는 간결한 문장들이 오래 곱씹을 거리를 준다.
aboutEn: A collection of short chapters attributed to Laozi, opening with the claim that the Tao that can be named is not the enduring Tao. Its spare lines on names, opposites and effortless governing reward slow rereading.

title: 논어
author: 공자
match: The Analects of Confucius (from the Chinese Classics)
opening: CHAPTER I. 1. The Master said, 'Is it not pleasant to learn with a constant perseverance and application? 2. 'Is it not delightful to have friends coming from distant quarters?' 3. 'Is he not a man of complete virtue, who feels no discomposure though men may take no note of him?' CHAP. II. 1.
about: 공자와 제자들의 말과 대화를 모은 유교의 기본 경전으로, 레게(Legge)의 영역본이다. 배움의 즐거움을 말하는 첫 장부터 일상의 덕을 묻는 짧은 문답이 이어져 군자의 모습을 그려 볼 수 있다.
aboutEn: The core Confucian collection of sayings and exchanges between Confucius and his disciples, in James Legge's translation. Beginning with the joy of learning, its short passages build a picture of the "superior man."

title: 방법서설
author: 르네 데카르트
match: Discourse on the Method of Rightly Conducting One's Reason and of Seeking Truth in the Sciences
opening: Good sense is, of all things among men, the most equally distributed; for every one thinks himself so abundantly provided with it, that those even who are the most difficult to satisfy in everything else, do not usually desire a larger measure of this quality than they already possess.
about: 데카르트가 올바르게 이성을 쓰고 학문에서 진리를 구하는 방법을 자신의 지적 여정과 함께 여섯 부로 풀어 쓴 글이다. 양식이 누구에게나 고르게 주어졌다는 첫머리에서 출발해 의심하며 생각하는 방식을 따라가 볼 수 있다.
aboutEn: Descartes's account in six parts of how to use reason well and seek truth in the sciences, set within the story of his own thinking. Starting from the claim that good sense is equally shared, it lets you follow a method built on doubt.

title: 순수이성비판
author: 이마누엘 칸트
opening: Human reason, in one sphere of its cognition, is called upon to consider questions, which it cannot decline, as they are presented by its own nature, but which it cannot answer, as they transcend every faculty of the mind. It falls into this difficulty without any fault of its own.
about: 칸트가 인간 이성이 경험 없이 무엇을 알 수 있는지, 그 가능성과 한계를 따져 묻는 철학서다.
aboutEn: Kant examines what human reason can know independently of experience, and where the limits of that knowledge lie.

title: 차라투스트라는 이렇게 말했다
author: 프리드리히 니체
match: Thus Spake Zarathustra: A Book for All and None
opening: "Zarathustra" is my brother's most personal work; it is the history of his most individual experiences, of his friendships, ideals, raptures, bitterest disappointments and sorrows. Above it all, however, there soars, transfiguring it, the image of his greatest hopes and remotest aims.
about: 예언자 차라투스트라가 산에서 내려와 사람들에게 건네는 연설과 우화를 모은 니체의 책이다.
aboutEn: Nietzsche's book gathers the speeches and parables of the prophet Zarathustra as he comes down from the mountain to address people.

title: 선악의 저편
author: 프리드리히 니체
opening: SUPPOSING that Truth is a woman—what then? Is there not ground for suspecting that all philosophers, in so far as they have been dogmatists, have failed to understand women—that the terrible seriousness and clumsy importunity with which they have usually paid their addresses to Truth, have been unsk
about: 니체가 철학자들의 편견과 도덕의 내력을 짧은 단상과 아포리즘으로 파고드는 책이다.
aboutEn: Nietzsche probes the prejudices of philosophers and the history of morals through short, sharp aphorisms.

title: 종교적 경험의 다양성
author: 윌리엄 제임스
match: The Varieties of Religious Experience: A Study in Human Nature
opening: My thanks for help in writing these lectures are due to Edwin D. Starbuck, of Stanford University, who made over to me his large collection of manuscript material; to Henry W.
about: 윌리엄 제임스가 에든버러 기퍼드 강연에서 회심, 신비 체험 같은 종교적 경험을 심리학으로 살핀 스무 편의 강의다.
aboutEn: William James's twenty Gifford Lectures study religious experience such as conversion and mysticism from a psychological angle.

title: 에티카
author: 바뤼흐 스피노자
opening: I. By that which is self—caused, I mean that of which the essence involves existence, or that of which the nature is only conceivable as existent. II.
about: 스피노자가 자기원인, 실체, 속성, 신 같은 정의에서 출발해 기하학 방식으로 논증을 쌓아가는 책이다.
aboutEn: Spinoza builds his argument in geometrical fashion, starting from definitions of self-cause, substance, attribute and God.

title: 실용주의
author: 윌리엄 제임스
match: Pragmatism: A New Name for Some Old Ways of Thinking
opening: The lectures that follow were delivered at the Lowell Institute in Boston in November and December, 1906, and in January, 1907, at Columbia University, in New York. They are printed as delivered, without developments or notes.
about: 윌리엄 제임스가 1906~07년 강연에서 실용주의를 낡은 사유 방식의 새 이름으로 소개한 책이다.
aboutEn: In lectures given in 1906-07, William James presents pragmatism as a new name for some old ways of thinking.

title: 꿈의 해석
author: 지크문트 프로이트
opening: In attempting a discussion of the Interpretation of Dreams, I do not believe that I have overstepped the bounds of neuropathological interest.
about: 프로이트가 꿈이 어떻게 만들어지는지 심리 연구로 풀어낸 책이며, 브릴의 영어 번역본이다.
aboutEn: Freud investigates how dreams are formed through psychological study, here in A. A. Brill's English translation.

title: 공리주의
author: 존 스튜어트 밀
opening: There are few circumstances among those which make up the present condition of human knowledge, more unlike what might have been expected, or more significant of the backward state in which speculation on the most important subjects still lingers, than the little progress which has been made in the
about: 존 스튜어트 밀이 옳고 그름의 기준을 공리의 원리로 설명하고 정의와의 관계까지 다룬 짧은 윤리학 책이다.
aboutEn: John Stuart Mill's short work on ethics explains the principle of utility as the criterion of right and wrong, and its relation to justice.

title: 인간 지성에 관한 탐구
author: 데이비드 흄
opening: 1. Moral philosophy, or the science of human nature, may be treated after two different manners; each of which has its peculiar merit, and may contribute to the entertainment, instruction, and reformation of mankind.
about: 인간 본성을 다루는 도덕철학의 두 방식을 구분하며 시작해, 관념의 기원과 인과, 자유와 필연을 따지는 흄의 철학서다.
aboutEn:
Hume's philosophical work opens by distinguishing two ways of treating human nature, then examines the origin of ideas, causation, liberty and necessity.
It invites readers to ask how much of what we claim to know rests on habit rather than reason.

title: 파이돈
author: 플라톤
opening: After an interval of some months or years, and at Phlius, a town of Peloponnesus, the tale of the last hours of Socrates is narrated to Echecrates and other Phliasians by Phaedo the 'beloved disciple.' The Dialogue necessarily takes the form of a narrative, because Socrates has to be described actin
about: 소크라테스가 처형되는 날 제자들과 나눈 마지막 대화를 파이돈이 에케크라테스에게 전하는 형식의 대화편이다.
aboutEn:
A dialogue in which Phaedo tells Echecrates of the last hours of Socrates, spent in conversation with his disciples before his execution.
It shows how a philosopher spends his final day, and what he thinks of death.

title: 크리톤
author: 플라톤
opening: The Crito seems intended to exhibit the character of Socrates in one light only, not as the philosopher, fulfilling a divine mission and trusting in the will of heaven, but simply as the good citizen, who having been unjustly condemned is willing to give up his life in obedience to the laws of the s
about: 감옥에 갇힌 소크라테스에게 친구 크리톤이 새벽에 찾아와 탈옥을 권하는 장면에서 시작하는 플라톤의 대화편이다.
aboutEn:
A Platonic dialogue that begins before dawn, when Crito visits the imprisoned Socrates and urges him to escape.
It asks whether a citizen unjustly condemned still owes obedience to the laws.

title: 세네카 소론집
author: 세네카
match: Minor Dialogues, Together With the Dialogue on Clemency
